name: 2-to-4 Line Decoder
title: 2-to-4 Line Decoder
summary: A Decoder converts N binary address input lines into 2^N unique active output lines. A 2-to-4 decoder decodes address inputs A1 A0 into outputs Y0, Y1, Y2, Y3.

images.title: 2-to-4 Decoder Symbol
images.caption: Inputs A1, A0 and Outputs Y0, Y1, Y2, Y3.

working_principle: Outputs: Y0 = A1'·A0', Y1 = A1'·A0, Y2 = A1·A0', Y3 = A1·A0. Exactly one output line is HIGH (1) for each binary input combination.
applications: RAM/ROM Memory Address Decoding & Chip Select Lines
advantages: Enables address selection among multiple peripheral devices
disadvantages: Requires large gate networks for wide address buses (3-to-8, 4-to-16)
common_mistakes: Confusing active-high outputs (1 active) with active-low outputs (0 active).
quick_notes: N inputs decode into 2^N output lines.
Built using 2 NOT (7404) and 4 AND (7408) gates.

viva_questions.q: How many outputs does a 3-to-8 Line Decoder have?

interview_questions.q: How can a 3-to-8 Decoder be constructed using two 2-to-4 Decoders?
interview_questions.a: Connect the lower 2 address bits to both decoders and use the MSB address bit to enable/disable each decoder via an Enable pin.
